How do I install colcon on Ubuntu?.base:
To install colcon on Ubuntu, you can follow these steps:

1. Update the package list: `sudo apt update`
2. Install colcon: `sudo apt install colcon`
3. Verify the installation: `colcon --version`

Alternatively, you can install colcon using pip, which is the recommended method:

1. Install pip: `sudo apt install python3-pip`
2. Install colcon: `pip3 install colcon`
3. Verify the installation: `colcon --version`

Note: Make sure you have Python 3.8 or later installed on your system, as colcon requires Python 3.8 or later to run.

To build only one specific package using colcon, you can use the `--packages-select` flag followed by the name of the package you want to build.

For example, if you want to build only the `my_package` package, you can use the following command:
```
colcon build --packages-select my_package
```
This will build only the `my_package` package and its dependencies, without building any other packages.

Note that you can also use the `--build-base` flag to specify a specific package and its dependencies to build, like this:
```
colcon build --build-base my_package
```

What does the --symlink-install flag do.base:
The `--symlink-install` flag in colcon (CMake-based build and package management system for ROS2) is used to control how packages are installed.

When `--symlink-install` is set to `True` (which is the default), colcon creates symbolic links to the installed packages in the `install` directory. This means that the actual package files are not copied to the `install` directory, but instead, a symbolic link is created that points to the original package location.
